chunks: ʿAlī, from his father, from al-Nawfalī, from al-Sakūnī, from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said:

Amīr al-Muʾminīn عليه السلام said: “If the immoral woman is asked, ‘Who committed fornication with you?’ and she says, ‘So-and-so,’ then upon her are two hadd punishments: one hadd for her immorality, and one hadd for her false accusation against the Muslim man.”

key_terms.الرَّجُلِ الْمُسْلِمِ: the Muslim man against whom the accusation is made
key_terms.الْفَاجِرَةُ: the immoral woman; here, a woman guilty of illicit sexual conduct
key_terms.فُجُورِهَا: her immorality or illicit sexual conduct

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if a fornicating woman names a Muslim man as her partner without valid proof?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling concerning a woman guilty of fornication who accuses a specific Muslim man without the proof required by the Sacred Law. It states that she incurs two hadd punishments: one for her own immoral act and another for slandering the Muslim man through false accusation.
